label_note: Synthetic paired cases with team-reviewed labels written before any model run. Not an external expert assessment.

case.mechanism: Allosteric TYK2 inhibition via the JH2 pseudokinase domain, blocking IL-23, IL-12 and type I interferon signalling
case.program_data: SYN-TYK-201 is an oral JH2-binding TYK2 inhibitor. Candidate-specific preclinical PK and 28-day rat/dog GLP toxicology are complete; a Phase 1 SAD/MAD study in healthy volunteers is ongoing.

sources.title: Synthetic: TYK2 P1104A variant association study
Synthetic: TYK2 JH2 selectivity in human primary T cells
Synthetic: Phase 3 results of a first-in-class allosteric TYK2 inhibitor

evidence.excerpt: Carriers of the TYK2 P1104A partial loss-of-function variant had a lower risk of psoriasis and other immune-mediated diseases in population genetic association studies, without an increase in serious infection signals.
limitations: Association data; partial loss of function does not model full pharmacological inhibition.

evidence.excerpt: In human primary T cells, selective TYK2 JH2 binding reduced IL-23-induced STAT3 phosphorylation and IL-12-induced STAT4 phosphorylation while sparing JAK1/JAK3-dependent IL-2 signalling.
limitations: Ex vivo system.

evidence.excerpt: A first-in-class allosteric TYK2 inhibitor achieved superiority over placebo on PASI 75 at week 16 in randomized Phase 3 trials in plaque psoriasis.
limitations: Different chemotype from SYN-TYK-201.

evidence.excerpt: In 28-day GLP studies, SYN-TYK-201 showed no adverse liver findings in rats or dogs at exposures up to 10-fold the projected human efficacious AUC.
limitations: Animal toxicology does not establish human safety.

added_sources.title: Synthetic: SYN-TYK-201 Phase 1 MAD interim safety report

added_evidence.excerpt: In the SYN-TYK-201 Phase 1 MAD cohort at 300 mg once daily, 3 of 8 healthy participants developed ALT elevations above 5x ULN by day 10, leading to cohort discontinuation; elevations resolved after withdrawal. No ALT elevations occurred at 25-100 mg, where exposure remained below the projected efficacious AUC.
limitations: Interim data; n=8 per cohort; healthy volunteers, not psoriasis patients.

added_evidence.excerpt: Metabolite profiling identified a reactive acyl-glucuronide metabolite unique to the SYN-TYK-201 scaffold; covalent protein adducts were detected in human hepatocytes. The metabolite is not formed by the other TYK2 inhibitor chemotypes tested.
limitations: Causal attribution rests on in vitro adduct data.

changed_claims.changed_premise: Candidate-specific dose-limiting hepatotoxicity now contradicts safe human exposure at the projected efficacious level.
No tolerated SYN-TYK-201 dose reached projected efficacious exposure, so the candidate window is not demonstrated.
Human PK now exists but tolerated exposures sit below the projected efficacious AUC.
Clean rat/dog toxicology is superseded by human ALT elevations; liver safety monitoring and stopping rules become gating.
Next milestone moves from Phase 2 PASI efficacy to a backup chemotype without the reactive metabolite.

critical_facts: Dose-limiting ALT elevation in 3 of 8 participants at 300 mg QD; reversible on withdrawal.
Tolerated doses did not reach projected efficacious exposure.
Hepatotoxicity is attributed to a scaffold-specific reactive metabolite, not to TYK2 inhibition.
critical_risks: Program-level: SYN-TYK-201 may be non-developable at efficacious exposure.
Approach-level: competitive bar set by an approved allosteric TYK2 inhibitor.
acceptable_interpretations: Downgrade or redirect the program to a backup chemotype while keeping the TYK2 approach thesis.
Conditional recommendation gated on a metabolite-free backup reaching efficacious exposure.
unacceptable_interpretations: The TYK2 mechanism is invalidated by this candidate failure.
Clean rat/dog toxicology establishes human liver safety.
Low tolerated doses are both safe and efficacious.
limitations: Interim healthy-volunteer data with eight participants per cohort.
Metabolite causality inferred from in vitro hepatocyte adducts.

case.indication: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency-associated liver disease (PiZZ genotype)
case.mechanism: Hepatocyte-targeted GalNAc-siRNA silencing of SERPINA1 to reduce hepatic Z-AAT polymer accumulation
case.program_data: SYN-AAT-301 is a GalNAc-siRNA targeting SERPINA1 mRNA. PiZ mouse and cynomolgus pharmacology are complete; a Phase 1/2 study in PiZZ adults with liver involvement is enrolling.

sources.title: Synthetic: SYN-AAT-301 in PiZ transgenic mice

evidence.excerpt: Hepatic accumulation of misfolded Z-AAT polymers drives proteotoxic hepatocyte injury and fibrosis in PiZZ individuals; reducing Z-AAT synthesis is the mechanistic rationale for liver protection.
In PiZ transgenic mice, SYN-AAT-301 reduced hepatic SERPINA1 mRNA by 90% and decreased PAS-D-positive globule burden and liver fibrosis markers after 12 weeks.
limitations: Transgenic mouse model overexpresses human Z-AAT.

evidence.excerpt: In cynomolgus monkeys, single subcutaneous doses produced dose-dependent serum AAT reduction lasting more than 8 weeks.
limitations: Wild-type AAT; no disease phenotype.

added_evidence.excerpt: In PiZZ adult participants, SYN-AAT-301 reduced serum Z-AAT by a median of 87% at week 12 at the 200 mg dose, with dose-dependent reductions across cohorts; intrahepatic Z-AAT on paired liver biopsy decreased by a median of 70% at week 24 (n=6).
limitations: Paired biopsies in six participants; no fibrosis-stage endpoint yet.

added_evidence.excerpt: Over 24 weeks of follow-up, no treatment-related serious adverse events were reported; follow-up is insufficient to assess long-term hepatic or pulmonary outcomes.
limitations: 24-week follow-up; small cohorts.

changed_claims.changed_premise: Human target engagement is now shown by dose-dependent serum and intrahepatic Z-AAT reduction in PiZZ participants.
Intrahepatic polymer reduction is a proximal biological response; fibrosis regression is not yet shown.
Serum and intrahepatic Z-AAT are now validated pharmacodynamic markers for dose selection, not surrogates of clinical benefit.

critical_facts: Median serum Z-AAT reduction of 87% at week 12 (200 mg) and 70% intrahepatic reduction at week 24 (n=6).
No fibrosis-stage or clinical outcome data yet.
critical_risks: Long-term hepatic and pulmonary safety remain unknown after 24 weeks.
Silencing SERPINA1 lowers circulating AAT and may not protect, or may further expose, the lung.
Regulatory acceptance of histologic surrogate endpoints is uncertain.
acceptable_interpretations: Translation gap at target engagement is closed; patient benefit and long-term safety remain open.
Next milestone is histologic fibrosis improvement in a controlled study.
unacceptable_interpretations: Absence of serious adverse events over 24 weeks establishes long-term safety.
Positive PD data remove the pulmonary risk.
limitations: Interim, open-label data with small biopsy subset.
No comparator arm.

case.mechanism: LPA1 receptor antagonism to block lysophosphatidic acid-driven fibroblast recruitment and vascular leak

sources.title: Synthetic: BAL lysophosphatidic acid in IPF
Synthetic: LPA1-deficient mice in bleomycin fibrosis
Synthetic: Phase 2 LPA1 antagonist trial in IPF

evidence.excerpt: Bronchoalveolar lavage LPA concentrations were elevated in patients with IPF compared with controls and correlated with fibroblast chemotactic activity.
limitations: Correlative; cross-sectional.

evidence.excerpt: LPA1-deficient mice were protected from bleomycin-induced lung fibrosis, with reduced fibroblast accumulation and vascular leak.
limitations: Bleomycin model resolves spontaneously and imperfectly models IPF.

evidence.excerpt: In a 26-week randomized placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial, an LPA1 antagonist slowed the rate of FVC decline in patients with IPF.
limitations: FVC is a functional surrogate; 26 weeks.

added_evidence.excerpt: SYN-PD-33, an oral PDE4B inhibitor, showed dose-limiting gastrointestinal intolerance in a Phase 1 study in healthy volunteers.
limitations: Different candidate and mechanism.

added_evidence.excerpt: The sponsor announced a corporate name change and relocation of its clinical operations office; no study protocols or data were affected.
limitations: Administrative; no scientific content.

critical_facts: The new documents concern a PDE4B candidate and a corporate notice, not the LPA1 subject.
critical_risks: Human LPA1 receptor occupancy remains unmeasured.
FVC slowing over 26 weeks is a functional surrogate, not survival benefit.
acceptable_interpretations: No change to the LPA1 thesis; the documents are logged as irrelevant to the subject.
unacceptable_interpretations: PDE4B intolerance implies LPA1 antagonist intolerance.
A sponsor name change affects scientific or clinical risk.
limitations: Approach-scoped case; no candidate-specific program data.
